source_excerpts.text: What is Spatio-Temporal • “Spatio” refers to space, “temporal” refers to time. • Spatio-temporal (ST) , or spatial-temporal/ spatiotemporal/ space time/ space-time, is used in data analysis when data is collected across both space and time. • It describes a phenomenon in a certain location and time.

source_excerpts.text: Spatio-temporal cube structure • The spatio-temporal (ST) cube (时空立方体) is essentially a vector data structure, representing time and space with sampling point features. • Homogeneous or heterogeneous points are used to represent a specific time section or an aggregated feature. • When a number of time sections are combined together and symbolized as a cub for a series of point features, then ST cube data model is then constructed.

source_excerpts.text: Emerging Hot Spot Analysis • Emerging Hot Spot Analysis Tool identifies hot and cold spots and determines if they have a temporal trend (new versus persistent versus historic hot spots). • It finds trends in the clustering of point densities (counts) or values in a space-time NetCDF cube created using either the Create Space Time Cube By Aggregating Points, Create Space Time Cube From Defined Locations or Create Space Time Cube from Multidimensional Raster Layer tool.
source_excerpts.reason: Representative excerpt selected from the spatial-analysis knowledge base.

source_excerpts.text: Emerging Hot Spot Analysis • Uses the Conceptualization of Spatial Relationships values you provide to calculate the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic (Hot Spot Analysis) for each bin. • Once the space-time hot spot analysis completes, each bin in the input NetCDF cube has an associated z-score, p-value, and hot spot bin classification added to it. • Next, these hot and cold spot trends are evaluated using the Mann-Kendall trend test.
source_excerpts.reason: Representative excerpt selected from the spatial-analysis knowledge base.

source_excerpts.text: Mann-Kendall trend test • The Mann-Kendall trend test is performed on every location with data as an independent bin time-series test. The Mann-Kendall statistic is a rank correlation analysis for the bin count or value and their time sequence. • The bin value for the first time period is compared to the bin value for the second.
source_excerpts.reason: Representative excerpt selected from the spatial-analysis knowledge base.

source_excerpts.text: • Intensifying 在至少90%的时间(time step, 下同)内都具有显著统计意义 的热点，而且其具有高值的要素的数量持续增加。 • Persistent 在至少90%的时间内都具有显著统计意义的热点，其具有 高值的要素的数量无明显波动。 • Oscillating 在少于90%的时间内具有显著统计意义的热点，在某些时 间内可能是冷点。

source_excerpts.text: What is Spatio-Temporal • “Spatio” refers to space, “temporal” refers to time. • Spatio-temporal (ST) , or spatial-temporal/ spatiotemporal/ space time/ space-time, is used in data analysis when data is collected across both space and time. • It describes a phenomenon in a certain location and time.

source_excerpts.text: Spatio-temporal cube structure • The spatio-temporal (ST) cube (时空立方体) is essentially a vector data structure, representing time and space with sampling point features. • Homogeneous or heterogeneous points are used to represent a specific time section or an aggregated feature. • When a number of time sections are combined together and symbolized as a cub for a series of point features, then ST cube data model is then constructed.

source_excerpts.text: Emerging Hot Spot Analysis • Uses the Conceptualization of Spatial Relationships values you provide to calculate the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic (Hot Spot Analysis) for each bin. • Once the space-time hot spot analysis completes, each bin in the input NetCDF cube has an associated z-score, p-value, and hot spot bin classification added to it. • Next, these hot and cold spot trends are evaluated using the Mann-Kendall trend test.
source_excerpts.reason: Representative excerpt selected from the spatial-analysis knowledge base.

source_excerpts.text: Mann-Kendall trend test • The Mann-Kendall trend test is performed on every location with data as an independent bin time-series test. The Mann-Kendall statistic is a rank correlation analysis for the bin count or value and their time sequence. • The bin value for the first time period is compared to the bin value for the second.
